text.text: Vibeprint: how does an iPad sketch survive a page reload?
New engineers · Same-Wi-Fi link only (--no-relay or LAN URL): page reload, token cookie, WS snapshot, ink ops, canvas.json load/save.
iPad

Same Wi-Fi; holds HttpOnly
token cookie
Developer machine
Local, self-run; token-gated LAN HTTP/WS
iPad browser

Draws ink; unacked
ops in page memory
only
vibeprint serve

Token-gated; acks
ops in memory,
saves later
canvas.json

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient, response included;
dotted (local) = file/IPC; solid (sync) = awaited request/reply; dashed (async) = event/stream.
Acked is not saved

Ack means daemon memory only.
canvas.json is rewritten (temp file +
rename) after 800ms with no op from any
client, or on SIGINT/SIGTERM; a crash loses
acked edits since the last pause.
Source: src/server/canvas.ts
Reconnect replays; reload drops

Unacked ops live only in page memory: a
reconnect (500ms–10s backoff) replays
them on a fresh snapshot; a full reload loses
them. Rejected ops (invalid/full) drop; page
resnapshots.
Source: web/src/canvas/sync.ts
Token gate on reload

/ needs no token; /api/config and /api/canvas
WS need the ?t= link's 1-year HttpOnly
cookie (token kept across restarts). Without
it: 401, fixed 'needs the link' page, no retry.
Source: src/server/daemon.ts
Outside this view: Default hosted relay link (QR uses it when up), MCP, AI, git commits; Marks/chat/graph files, pasted images, other clients' live ops.
